The thing about ligamental strains and tears is you have to understand how they actually attach on the bone. Here's a picture of a fibro-osseous junction which is the point at which a ligament/tendon attaches to the bone. Each bone has a place on it where the muscle tendons and ligaments attach. The attachment point for example of your bicep can be found on the forearm and shoulder, specifically at the coracoid process and inserts into the tubercle of the Radius.

So as a body part moves, the ligaments and tendons stretch pulling on these points. But given enough time, without rest and these ligaments and tendons get strained. The fact that children as young as 4-6 are able to play pee-wee league... well it creates a stress on the body that isn't designed for it to handle.

In exercise we talk about overtraining. Giving the body enough time to rest is important. The body needs time to heal and to recover. The nervous system gets excited and produces a greater impulse which in turn creates even more strain on the attachment points.
